response.title: how to keep security cameras and the alarm working during a power outage
response.answer:
The most reliable way to keep your security cameras and alarm system running during a power outage is to install a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) or a dedicated battery backup.

The right setup depends on whether your cameras use PoE (Power over Ethernet), Wi-Fi, or individual power adapters.

1. Recommended backup setup
Illustrative setup. The UPS must have enough capacity for the combined equipment load.

For most wired security systems, connect these devices to battery-backed outlets:

PoE switch: Powers PoE cameras.

NVR/DVR: Keeps video recording during the outage.

Router and modem/ONT: Maintain network connectivity.

Alarm control panel: Keeps sensors, sirens, and monitoring operational if compatible.

An alarm panel may already have its own backup battery. Check its age and rated runtime before adding external backup power.

2. How long can a UPS run your cameras?

Here are approximate runtimes for different usable battery capacities, assuming a combined 100-watt load.

Usable battery energy

	

Approx. runtime




100 Wh

	

1 hour




300 Wh

	

3 hours




500 Wh

	

5 hours




1,000 Wh

	

10 hours




2,000 Wh

	

20 hours

These are estimates. Actual runtime depends on UPS efficiency, battery condition, and equipment consumption.

*Assumes 80% of rated battery energy is available to equipment, including conversion losses and reserve. Verify the manufacturer's runtime chart and output wattage rating.
3. Choose the backup method
Shop

Standard UPS

Best for short outages (minutes to a few hours, depending on load). Automatically switches to battery power and is relatively easy to install.

Shop

Large battery power station with UPS/EPS functionality

Better for outages lasting many hours. Verify automatic transfer time and compatibility with your equipment; not all power stations provide uninterrupted power.

Shop

DC mini UPS

Useful for individual Wi-Fi cameras, routers, or compatible alarm devices. Match voltage, connector polarity, and current requirements.

4. Don't forget internet and alarm monitoring

Keeping the equipment powered does not necessarily mean it stays connected.

Your internet provider's network may also lose power, even when your router is backed up.

A cellular LTE/5G backup can maintain alarm monitoring and some remote camera access.

Local NVR recording can continue without internet if the cameras, PoE switch, and recorder remain powered.

Test the setup by safely disconnecting the UPS from wall power and checking camera recording, alarm status, and remote access.

The most reliable way to keep your **security cameras and alarm system running during a power outage** is to install a **UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)** or a dedicated battery backup.

The right setup depends on whether your cameras use PoE (Power over Ethernet), Wi-Fi, or individual power adapters.

## 1. Recommended backup setup

For most wired security systems, connect these devices to battery-backed outlets:

- **PoE switch:** Powers PoE cameras.
- **NVR/DVR:** Keeps video recording during the outage.
- **Router and modem/ONT:** Maintain network connectivity.
- **Alarm control panel:** Keeps sensors, sirens, and monitoring operational if compatible.

An alarm panel may already have its own backup battery. Check its age and rated runtime before adding external backup power.

## 2. How long can a UPS run your cameras?

Here are approximate runtimes for different usable battery capacities, assuming a combined 100-watt load.

| Usable battery energy | Approx. runtime |
|---|---|
| 100 Wh | 1 hour |
| 300 Wh | 3 hours |
| 500 Wh | 5 hours |
| 1,000 Wh | 10 hours |
| 2,000 Wh | 20 hours |

These are estimates. Actual runtime depends on UPS efficiency, battery condition, and equipment consumption.

{@body const [cameras,setCameras] = DIL.useState(4)}
{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(8)}
{@body const [other,setOther] = DIL.useState(45)}
{@body const [hours,setHours] = DIL.useState(8)}
{@body const load = cameras*watts+other}
{@body const energy = Math.ceil(load*hours/0.8)}

        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Required rated energy*</text>
        <title size="xl" tabularNums>{energy.toLocaleString()} Wh</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <caption>*Assumes 80% of rated battery energy is available to equipment, including conversion losses and reserve. Verify the manufacturer's runtime chart and output wattage rating.</caption>
</box>

## 3. Choose the backup method

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="APC Back UPS battery backup tower UPS 1500VA" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="124px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Standard UPS**

      Best for short outages (minutes to a few hours, depending on load). Automatically switches to battery power and is relatively easy to install.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="LiFePO4 portable power station EcoFlow Delta battery" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="124px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Large battery power station with UPS/EPS functionality**

      Better for outages lasting many hours. Verify automatic transfer time and compatibility with your equipment; not all power stations provide uninterrupted power.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="12V DC mini UPS battery backup router security camera" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="124px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **DC mini UPS**

      Useful for individual Wi-Fi cameras, routers, or compatible alarm devices. Match voltage, connector polarity, and current requirements.
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## 4. Don't forget internet and alarm monitoring

Keeping the equipment powered does not necessarily mean it stays connected.

- Your internet provider's network may also lose power, even when your router is backed up.
- A cellular LTE/5G backup can maintain alarm monitoring and some remote camera access.
- Local NVR recording can continue without internet if the cameras, PoE switch, and recorder remain powered.
- Test the setup by safely disconnecting the UPS from wall power and checking camera recording, alarm status, and remote access.

  </form>
